fields.h1: Build a Manager Feedback Survey for Teams and Their Managers
fields.hero_description: Build a manager feedback survey that gives each manager a private report and pools small teams so no one stands out.
fields.features_heading: What Each Manager's Survey Comes With
fields.features_subheading: A manager feedback survey asks direct reports to rate the person they report to, then gives that manager a private report.
fields.feature_1:
Statements about the person you report to

Emergent writes each statement about one manager, such as "My manager keeps our 1:1s as planned." Ask for changes by prompt until the wording sounds like your own teams.
fields.feature_2:
A private report for each manager

Each manager opens a report on their own team only, with the lowest-scoring statement at the top and the written comments under it. No other manager can open that report.
fields.feature_3:
A minimum count before any team shows

Set the smallest team a report may show, such as 3 answers. A team under that line still counts toward the director's rollup and the company total, but never shows alone.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders that stop after an answer

People who have not answered get an email reminder before the survey closes, and HR gets a Slack list of teams still under the minimum. Anyone finished gets no more email.
fields.feature_5:
One statement per screen on a phone

Staff in a clinic or on a warehouse floor answer one statement per screen from a link on their phone. Emergent puts no cap on responses, so 40 teams run on the same build.
fields.feature_6:
Your code on GitHub, answers in your tables

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Every answer already sits in a database you own, so next spring's round compares against this year's scores.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Teams Run Manager Feedback
fields.tab_content_1:
Her report opens on 1:1s, the lowest item

Halvorsen Dental's 9 hygienists rate practice manager Odile Brask on 8 statements, and 8 of 9 answered this round. Her private report opens on the lowest item, 1:1s held as planned, at 2.6. Praise for good work scored highest, at 4.1. She moved her 1:1s to Tuesday mornings and told the team why at the next huddle.
fields.tab_content_2:
Two small teams fold into a combined row

Sela Marquand directs 6 warehouse managers at Marlpit Logistics, and her rollup shows each team's answer count and average. The 2 teams with fewer than 3 answers share one combined row, and neither can be read alone. Night dock has the lowest average, at 3.1, and Sela booked a skip-level meeting there.
fields.tab_content_3:
Six weeks after his promise, 6 of 7 agree

Rui Okafor's team at Tessaly Software rated focus time lowest in the spring round, and he made Wednesdays meeting-free. Six weeks later, the app sent his 7 reports 2 statements. On "I get uninterrupted time for deep work," 6 of 7 agreed, up from 2 of 7 in spring.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any Not yet on a new hire emails HR

On day 45, every manager at Brightfern Clinics answers 5 questions about each new hire. One asks whether the hire is ready to work shifts alone: Yes, Not yet, or Too early to say. A Not yet emails HR partner Dana Whitcomb with the manager's comment. Of 14 October hires, 2 drew a Not yet.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Manager Feedback Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to run a manager feedback survey that each manager reads in private and acts on, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick the smallest team a report shows
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down who sees what before anything goes out. One split that works: each manager reads their own team's report, a director sees the rollup, and HR sees everything. Put that split in the invitation in one plain sentence.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose the answer count below which a team's results never appear on their own, such as 3. Teams under it fold into the director's rollup. Check the build applies the line to comments and exports before anyone answers.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write 8 to 12 statements about actions a direct report can see, like holding 1:1s, explaining priorities, and giving credit. Skip traits such as "is a good leader." Describe the list in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the statements.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask what the manager should keep doing and what they should change. These two comments give a low score its reason. Keep them optional, since a small team can sometimes guess who wrote a distinctive answer.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Send it in a quiet stretch
fields.howto_step_5_des: Avoid the weeks around performance reviews, when people may trade a rating for a rating. Leave the survey open for about 10 working days, with one reminder near the end for anyone who has not answered.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Give each manager their report first
fields.howto_step_6_des: Release reports to managers a few days before the director's rollup meeting. Ask each manager to pick one statement to work on and tell the team which one it is at their next meeting. Saying it aloud turns a private score into a promise the team can check.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Six weeks later, resend only the statement the manager chose, worded exactly as before. Identical wording is what makes the two scores comparable, and the team sees that what it wrote in the first round led somewhere.

faq_plan.q: What is a manager feedback survey?
faq_plan.a: A manager feedback survey is a short survey in which a team rates its own manager on everyday behaviors, such as holding 1:1s or explaining priorities. It is one form of upward feedback, where staff give feedback about their supervisor. Names stay off the answers, and each manager sees results for their own team only.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a manager feedback survey?
faq_plan.a: Decide who reads each report and how many answers a team needs before its results show. Then draft about 10 statements on things a manager does, plus two optional comment boxes. Describe that plan to Emergent's AI survey builder, and it builds the survey, each manager's report, and the response database as one app.

faq_plan.q: What are good manager feedback survey questions to ask?
faq_plan.a: Good manager feedback survey questions name one behavior the team can see. Try "My manager holds our 1:1s as planned," "My manager explains why priorities change," and "My manager gives credit for good work," each rated on an agree scale. Avoid doubled items like "communicates and supports": a score of 3 cannot tell you which half fell short.

faq_plan.q: What are some manager feedback survey examples?
faq_plan.a: Four manager feedback survey examples appear on this page. Hygienists rate their practice manager, a director reads a rollup across teams, a team answers a short recheck after its manager's change, and a manager answers questions about a new hire at day 45. That last one pairs well with an onboarding survey the new hire answers in the same week.

faq_plan.q: How do manager feedback surveys stay anonymous on a small team?
faq_plan.a: Manager feedback surveys stay anonymous by setting a minimum answer count before a team's results appear. At Emory University, a supervisor's leader will only receive the feedback if three or more direct reports complete the questionnaire. Leave name and email fields off the survey as well, and keep comment boxes optional.

faq_plan.q: Can I compare manager feedback survey scores across rounds?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when each statement and its scale stay the same between rounds. Save every round with its date and the team it covers, and the report can show this spring's 1:1s score beside last fall's for the same manager. With Emergent, each round lands in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can a manager feedback survey show why people leave a team?
faq_plan.a: It can show early warning signs while people are still on the team, such as a falling score on workload or on 1:1s. It cannot say why one person left. Ask that in an exit survey near the last day, then compare its themes with that team's last manager round.

faq_plan.q: Should manager feedback survey results affect a manager's performance review?
faq_plan.a: Keep them out of pay and ratings for the first two rounds at least. Use the results to set one development goal per manager, and say so in the invitation. People write more plainly when they know a manager's raise does not ride on what they say.

faq_plan.q: How do I get more people to answer a manager feedback survey?
faq_plan.a: Tell people what changed after the last round before the new one opens, even if it was one thing. Keep the survey near 10 statements. Then give each team 10 minutes of a regular meeting to answer, with the manager out of the room.

faq_plan.q: Should a manager feedback survey run on its own or inside a company-wide survey?
faq_plan.a: Run it on its own when you want a report per manager. A company-wide employee engagement survey can carry 2 or 3 manager statements, but that is too few to show a manager what to change. With no response cap in Emergent, both surveys can go to every employee.

plan.angle: The searches behind this primary want the questions to ask about a manager and a way to run the survey. Question lists and template pages stop at the list. This page shows the loop around one manager: the team rates its own manager and the manager reads a private report led by the lowest item, a director sees every manager on one screen with teams under 3 answers pooled, the one change a manager commits to is rechecked six weeks later, and the reverse direction, a manager answering about a new hire at day 45. scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Manager Feedback Survey for Teams and Their Managers'; hero 'Build a manager feedback survey that gives each manager a private report and pools small teams so no one stands out.' (under 130 chars, carries the primary, leads with Build); how-to description 'Seven steps to run a manager feedback survey that each manager reads in private and acts on, then build it with Emergent.'

intent.evidence: Delivers example statements ('My manager holds our 1:1s as planned,' 'My manager explains why priorities change'), four worked examples (FAQ 4 lists them), a seven-step how-to and anonymity on small teams (FAQ 5), which is what a 'manager feedback survey' / 'questions' / 'examples' searcher wants.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'skip-level', 'rollup', '1:1s held as planned', 'Teams under it fold into the director's rollup', 'day 45'; table generated from the library.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'Halvorsen Dental's 9 hygienists rate practice manager Odile Brask on 8 statements', 'Write down who sees what before anything goes out.', 'Emergent writes each statement about one manager'.

craft.evidence: Short declaratives, one idea each: 'Skip traits such as "is a good leader."' Two ', so' endings (features 5 and 6) sit at the limit; recorded as a note.

voice.evidence: Operator detail, no hype: 'She moved her 1:1s to Tuesday mornings and told the team why at the next huddle.' 'Avoid the weeks around performance reviews, when people may trade a rating for a rating.'

truth.evidence: Both third-party facts match the Emory source spans: FAQ 1 'one form of upward feedback, where staff give feedback about their supervisor' (source: 'Upward Feedback (Supervisor Feedback) ... provide feedback about their supervisor'); FAQ 5 'a supervisor's leader will only receive the feedback if three or more direct reports complete the questionnaire' (verbatim in source). Emergent claims map to prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, conversational, no-caps, code-export ('Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans'). Numbers agree across copy, mockups and images (8 of 9, 2.6, 4.1; 6 managers, 3.1, 2 pooled teams; 2 of 7 to 6 of 7; 14 hires, 2 Not yet).

distinct.evidence: No sibling primary in any heading (no 'leadership survey', '360 survey', 'team survey', 'onboarding survey'); tabs center on a line manager and direct reports, with tab 4 reversing direction. Overlap with leadership-survey tab 1 and 360-survey tab 3 recorded as a note.

faq.evidence: 10 written questions, gate pass 10/10 (hubctl paa --spec), no brands or formats, each answered in its first sentence ('Manager feedback surveys stay anonymous by setting a minimum answer count before a team's results appear.'); hub link in item 2, sibling links onboarding survey, exit survey, employee engagement survey; moat lines in FAQ 6 and 10. FAQ 8 is HR practice advice, not legal advice.

findings.quote: Six weeks later, resend only the statement the manager chose, worded exactly as before. / Six weeks later, the app sent his 7 reports 2 statements.
findings.issue: The how-to says to resend only the one chosen statement; the tab example on the same page resends 2 (chip add and mockup agree with the tab). Not a factual contradiction, but an attentive reader sees the page not following its own step.
findings.fix: Either let step 7 allow 'the statement or two the manager chose', or keep it as is; no rework.

findings.quote: Keep them out of pay and ratings for the first two rounds at least. ... People write more plainly when they know a manager's raise does not ride on what they say. / Avoid the weeks around performance reviews, when people may trade a rating for a rating.

findings.fix: Optional: a source on keeping upward feedback developmental (for example an HR body's guidance) if the page is revised.
